reference: Moist-air states from CoolProp 8.0.0 HAPropsSI (ASHRAE RP-1485 real-gas formulation) cross-checked against a closed-form implementation of Bolton (1980) eq. 10 and ASHRAE Handbook - Fundamentals (2021) ch. 1 eq. 20, 32 and 33 written for this benchmark and solved by bisection to 1e-12 K; the catalogue sizing and the price build-up are recomputed independently in python from the assumptions the tool publishes and are graded as arithmetic identities.
reference_citations: ASHRAE Handbook - Fundamentals (2021), chapter 1 "Psychrometrics": eq. 20 (humidity ratio W = 0.621945 p_w/(p - p_w)), eq. 32 (moist-air specific enthalpy h = 1.006 t + W(2501 + 1.86 t) kJ per kg dry air) and eq. 33 (thermodynamic wet-bulb temperature).

D. Bolton, "The computation of equivalent potential temperature", Monthly Weather Review 108(7):1046-1053, 1980, eq. 10: e_s = 6.112 exp(17.67 T/(T + 243.5)) hPa, stated accurate to 0.1 % for -35 <= T <= +35 degC.
CoolProp 8.0.0, HAPropsSI; humid-air model of S. Herrmann, H.-J. Kretzschmar and D.P. Gatley, ASHRAE RP-1485 (2009), "Thermodynamic Properties of Real Moist Air".

R. Stull, "Wet-bulb temperature from relative humidity and air temperature", Journal of Applied Meteorology and Climatology 50(11):2267-2269, 2011 - the correlation the tool used before this pass; stated valid at standard sea-level pressure with errors from -1.0 to +0.65 K (RMS 0.28 K) for 5 % <= RH <= 99 %, -20 <= T <= +50 degC.
ASHRAE Handbook - Fundamentals (2021), chapter 1, eq. 35: cooling-coil load q = m_da[(h_1 - h_2) - (W_1 - W_2) h_w], the condensate leaving as saturated liquid at the coil surface temperature.
tolerance: Two references are used. Against the closed-form reference - the same published equations (Bolton 1980 eq.10; ASHRAE Fundamentals 2021 ch.1 eq.20, 32, 33 and 35) implemented independently in python and solved by bisection to 1e-12 K - the tool is held to 1e-9 relative, because nothing but floating point separates two evaluations of the same closed form; unit counts and feasibility flags must match exactly. Against CoolProp 8.0.0 (ASHRAE RP-1485 real moist air) the tolerance is the size of the approximation the tool declares, not what makes it pass: 0.6 % on the humidity ratio (the water-vapour enhancement factor the ideal-gas form omits, measured 0.49 %), 0.05 K on the thermodynamic wet bulb (measured 0.026 K), 0.1 % on the dry-air density (measured 0.039 %), 1 % on the coil load and 0.10 K on the constancy of the wet bulb along the evaporative path (measured 0.063 K). Bookkeeping identities - mass flow = density x volume flow, temperature rise = load / (mass flow x cp), running cost = energy x tariff + water x tariff + maintenance, lifetime cost = CAPEX + N x annual - are exact arithmetic and are held to 1e-9.
not_benchmarked: The Cairox catalogue itself (22000 m3/h / 3.0 kW supply unit, 31500 m3/h / 4.0 kW roof ARFV, 27855 m3/h / 2.2 kW wall axial) and every price in the build-up are supplier data, not physics; the harness checks they are applied consistently, never that they are right.
The design-day correction t_design = t_peak - 2.2 ln(1 + n/3) is an in-house correlation with no published provenance. Only its faithful implementation is checked.

The annual energy is a single design point multiplied by fixed load factors (fans and cooling at 0.5, an evaporative wet fraction (t_design - 20)/22 clamped to 0.2-0.85, PV at 0.45 kWh per kWp per operating hour). This is not a weather-bin or hourly aggregation and no attempt is made here to grade those factors against measured weather data.

The occupied-zone stratification fraction f = 0.5 + 0.5 z_work/H is a convention of this tool. It is energy-consistent at the roof extract, but it is not EN or ASHRAE-derived and is not benchmarked against measurement or CFD.
The adiabatic section and the cooling coil are assumed passive in the airstream: their pressure drop is not charged to the fans. That assumption is disclosed by the tool and is not graded here.
The chiller is represented by a single EER; part-load behaviour, condensing conditions and the reheat that a real dehumidifying coil often needs are outside the model.
The lifetime cost is an undiscounted sum; no annuity, interest rate or escalation is modelled, so there is no capital-annuity arithmetic to check.
run_notes: Driven through the tool's own permalink codec; every number read back from Diagram.record.build().

Cross-check between the two references over the 30 climate/load cases: humidity ratio agrees to 0.49 %, thermodynamic wet bulb to 0.026 K, dry-air density to 0.039 %, moist-air enthalpy to 0.043 %, and the wet bulb of the evaporative exit state reproduces the inlet wet bulb to 0.063 K.

Baseline before this pass: the mechanical coil load was the sensible part only (m cp dT), which understated the duty by a factor 1.17 at 32 degC/40 % RH rising to 3.04 at 34 degC/80 % RH, and the leaving humidity ratio was fixed at 95 % RH at 16 degC even when that was above the entering humidity ratio. The wet bulb came from the Stull (2011) correlation, which carries no pressure dependence at all.
crosscheck: closed form (Bolton/ASHRAE) vs CoolProp 8.0.0 over 30 cases: humidity ratio 0.49 %, wet bulb 0.026 K, dry-air density 0.039 %, enthalpy 0.043 %. The humidity ratio gap is the water-vapour enhancement factor that the ideal-gas form omits and is a property of the declared approximation, not of the tool.
